documented_differences.detail: The pilot decodes its decks to linear light and re-encodes inside the pass (`linearToSrgb(c)`); the editor's pictures are already sRGB-encoded bytes, so the grain is added to the encoded source directly. The same maths on the same colours.
The pilot writes alpha 1.0; the editor keeps the alpha of the picture it draws over. The cases pin it (grain-alpha-is-preserved).
`uGrain x uAmount <= 0` returns the source exactly in the pilot too (its output alpha aside); the identity cases pin the exact bytes.

The pilot's `withKeyAt` writes `easing: linear` on a new key; the editor leaves an easing nobody chose unwritten (it reads as linear) and an upsert that omits one keeps the key's own. The sampled values are the same.
A key at a negative frame is reported as KEY_OUT_OF_CLIP only (the pilot also reports KEYFRAME_ORDER); a fractional frame is INVALID_VALUE (the importer's own whole-number rule).
A clip shortened under one of its keys is refused atomically with KEY_OUT_OF_CLIP; the pilot's Studio drops the key with a note. The editor never discards data by a resize.

pixel_tolerance.why: the expectation is the unrounded float; the runtime reads 8-bit bytes and its pow may differ in the last bit of a half float. The noise itself is compared as exact integers (cell, hash, float32 bits), where the tolerance is zero.
